# `silk/raw_mapping`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Owned anonymous Linux mappings with runtime page-size and alignment checks.

## When to use

Use `Mapping.allocate` in a raw Linux composition after startup validates AT_PAGESZ.
Each successful value owns its entire mapping and releases it on structured drop.

## Gotchas

Raw pointers do not keep their mapping alive. Fatal traps do not guarantee release.

Import as `Mapping` with `import silk.raw_mapping { Mapping }`.

Public declarations: 1.

### Associated function `allocate`

```silk
pub fn allocate(length: usize, alignment: usize, pageSize: usize) -> Result<Mapping, usize>
```

Allocates a zero-initialized byte range with the requested alignment.

#### Details

The caller supplies the process page size from validated AT_PAGESZ. Size must be positive;
page size and alignment must be powers of two. Invalid values and arithmetic overflow return
error 22. Mapping failure returns the kernel error. Success owns one complete mapping.

<a id="declaration-"></a>

### Method `length`

```silk
pub fn length(self: &Mapping) -> usize
```

Returns the requested usable byte count, excluding alignment padding.

<a id="declaration-"></a>

### Method `pointer`

```silk
pub unsafe fn pointer(self: &mut Mapping) -> ?[*]mut u8
```

Returns the aligned address of the mapping's usable range.

#### Gotchas

The pointer grants no ownership. Keep the mapping alive and limit accesses to `length` bytes.
The initial bytes are zero; subsequent reads require the caller to preserve initialization.

<a id="declaration-"></a>

### Associated function `release`

```silk
pub fn release(value: Mapping) -> usize
```

Releases the complete mapping and consumes its owner.

#### Details

Returns zero on success or the positive kernel error. Drop makes no second release attempt.
